rules.scope: General amino-acid chemistry; used as design hypotheses for GB1, not as measured fitness effects
rules.action: Describe the chemical change of the side chain. Valine, methionine and alanine are examples of nonpolar side chains; serine, threonine and cysteine are examples of polar side chains.
rules.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 3.4 Proteins, Amino Acids: https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/3-4-proteins
rules.explanation: Side-chain chemistry may motivate a hypothesis, but it does not establish whether a substitution improves the GB1 assay.

rules.scope: General amino-acid chemistry; protonation depends on environment
rules.condition: A proposed substitution changes charge class
rules.action: Consider lysine and arginine as positively charged side-chain examples and aspartate and glutamate as negatively charged examples under typical biological conditions. State the proposed interaction and its uncertainty.
rules.explanation: Charge is a chemical descriptor, not a direction-of-fitness rule.

rules.scope: General amino-acid structure; no GB1-specific fitness claim
rules.condition: Introducing or replacing glycine or proline
rules.action: Discuss the small hydrogen side chain of glycine and the cyclic structure of proline when forming a structural hypothesis. Keep structural effects conditional without a structure-specific calculation.
rules.explanation: These chemical distinctions motivate experiments and do not impose a hard candidate filter.

rules.scope: Wu et al. 2016 GB1 four-site combinations at 39,40,41,54
rules.condition: Combining substitutions or interpreting marginal residue statistics
rules.action: Treat combined substitutions as a testable hypothesis. A favorable observation in one background need not transfer additively to another background; use only current-method known measurements and feedback when supporting a design.
rules.source: Wu et al. 2016, Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths: https://elifesciences.org/articles/16965 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4985287/
rules.explanation: The rule communicates epistasis without revealing high-fitness variants or hidden labels.
